column3: v52 298a: offering, consecration and Vajrasattva glosses all follow the Tibetan; "pacification of the commitment-being" for ཉེ་བར་ཞི་བའི་དམ་ཚིག་པ (the pacified samaya-being) is loose, not wrong.
v4 176a: the lamp/darkness simile, the dependent-arising of bliss through deity yoga and the root lemmas all follow the Tibetan; "possessive of dependence" (ལྟོས་དང་བཅས་པ) is clumsy only.

v92 62b: the chapter colophon, Subhūti's "perfection of non-existence", the space simile and the equality/seclusion lemmas all follow the Tibetan. The truncated opening list (མངོན་སུམ་དུ་མ་ཐོབ་པ …) depends on the previous side and cannot be judged here.

v133 277b: a Daśabhūmika-type list of the hundredfold powers, glossed lemma by lemma. "The vision of primordial wisdom enters even for a hundred eons" is literal (it sees into a hundred eons) but not wrong.
v95 143b: the synonym chain (inconceivable / unborn / dharmadhātu / without origin) and the gloss of དབྱིངས as རིགས are rendered faithfully.
v93 264b: the ten masteries, the three things a Tathāgata need not guard, and the 32 marks are all rendered faithfully; Sanskrit equivalents in the notes are correct.
v84 31b: the 25,000-line sūtra text on the signs of irreversibility in dreams follows the Tibetan closely (attendants for ཞམ་འབྲིང, "does not find satisfaction" for ལེགས་པའི་སེམས་མི་བསྐྱེད).

v157 148a: the Vinaya glosses on boats, seats and robes, the pātayantika numbering and the "no duṣkṛta" clause all follow the Tibetan. "mast" for གདོས་པ (= གསོག་ཤིང) is uncertain, but I cannot show it wrong.

v100 41a: the syllogism, the subject/probandum/probans/example parse and the opponent's "sound is impermanent because visible" parallel are right. One soft spot: དེ་ལ་ནི་རྣམ་པར་རྟོག་པ་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་འཛིན་པ་ཉིད་མེད་པས (form, lacking conceptuality, does no grasping) becomes "there is no 'perception' of it", which blurs who grasps; the next paragraph restores the sense.

v38 225b: the añjana rite (skulls, crossroads, wick, smoke, 108 recitations), the three siddhis and the Dīpaṃkara gloss follow the Tibetan; the "great oil" note (mahātaila as human fat) is a defensible reading of ཏིལ་མར་ཆེན་པོ.
